prompt: Hand a whole batch of Callables to an ExecutorService with invokeAll, then read the Futures back in input order. Complete checksums and largestChecksum, then run the tests.
explanation: invokeAll submits every Callable at once and blocks until all of them have finished, returning a List<Future> in exactly the same order as the tasks you passed in. Because the order is preserved you can loop over the Futures and call get() to build a result list that lines up with the input, even though the work ran on four threads in an unpredictable order. Calling shutdown() when you are done releases the pool threads, which are otherwise non-daemon and keep the JVM alive.
hints: Build a List<Callable<Integer>> first -- one Callable per word -- and only then call pool.invokeAll(tasks).
invokeAll returns List<Future<Integer>> in the same order as the tasks, so a plain for-each over that list and future.get() gives you results in input order.
Put pool.shutdown() in a finally block so the pool is released even when a task throws, and remember largestChecksum must return -1 rather than 0 for an empty list.
